what: `on.request.transaction: true` runs every SQL step of an HTTP flow in one database transaction: either everything the flow wrote is kept, or nothing is. The value is `true` or `false`. Left out it is `false`: each SQL statement commits as it runs, so a step that fails leaves the writes of the steps before it in place. `on.schedule.transaction: true` does the same for a scheduled flow (scheduled_transaction).
commit: The transaction commits when the steps end without a failed step and the answer could be produced. For a synchronous request the answer (status, headers and body, up to 1 MiB) is held back until the commit has succeeded. A respond step that renders is an answer whatever its status: `status: 409` written by the flow commits like a 200. A flow that ends without respond or redirect also commits, and answers the 500 `flow_no_response` (transactional_responses).
rollback: The transaction rolls back when a step fails (a SQL error, an `expect_rows` that does not hold, a `${{ }}` reference with no value, a failed outbound call: step_failures), when a respond or redirect step cannot produce its answer (transactional_responses), when the flow passes its time limit or the app's write-transaction limit (503 `flow_timeout` with `rolled_back: true`: time_limits), or when the commit itself fails. To undo the writes and still choose the answer, let a step fail and respond from its `on_error` handler: the handler runs after the rollback and its own writes are kept (error_handler_response).
rolled_back: Everything the flow wrote through the database: the rows written by `run: sql` and `run: sql_dynamic` steps at any depth (earlier `for_each` iterations included), the jobs queued by `run: enqueue` (a queued job runs only after COMMIT), the notifications written by `run: notify`, and the realtime events of those writes, which are sent only after COMMIT (realtime_events).
not_rolled_back: What has already left the database. `run: email`, `run: sms` and `run: webhook` send at once and are not undone; a write of the flow file warns about each one (transactional_sends), and `run: enqueue` is the way to send only after COMMIT. A `run: api` call already made, a `run: broadcast` message already delivered and a private upload already removed by `run: delete_upload` are not undone either. The writes of an `on_error` handler are outside the transaction.
limits: A transaction holds the app's one database write lock from its start to the commit, and every other write of the app waits for it (api({at:'recovery'}) write_lock): keep slow work such as outbound calls out of it, or before the first write. Refused in a `transaction: true` flow when the file is written: SQL steps inside `run: parallel` (parallel), `run: serve_file` (serve_file), `run: proxy` (proxy) and `run: extract_text`. A `timeout:` above the write-transaction limit (60 s by default) needs that limit raised too (time_limits). `run: purge_current_user` requires `transaction: true` (api({at:'auth'}) account_erasure).
async_and_retries: On a `mode: async` flow the job's steps run in one transaction when the job runs. With `on.request.max_attempts`, a failed run is rolled back and the next attempt starts a new transaction; the outbound effects of the failed run are repeated (api({at:'async-flows'}) retries).
